summary: Mount Philo's state fire tower: a 60-foot wood tower by 1924, replaced by an 80-foot steel tower in 1938, and found fallen from its base in February 1973.

facts.design: 60-foot wood tower with glass-enclosed top (by 1924); 80-foot steel tower with glass-enclosed cab (1938-40)
facts.status_note: Found fallen from its cement base in February 1973; no source describes remains on the summit.
facts.agency: Vermont Forest Service (built the tower); Vermont State Parks (summit today)

access.note: Mount Philo State Park. The summit access road reaches the top, and visitors can also climb to the summit on foot.

visit.trail_note: Visitors can park at the bottom and climb to the top, or drive to the summit.

events.note: Biennial report for 1924-26 says a new 60-foot tower with glass enclosure was erected; a November 1924 item already refers to the tower
The 60-foot wood tower was taken down; an 80-foot steel tower was delivered, to be erected by a CCC camp from Underhill
CCC built the steel tower with glass-enclosed cab; Civil Aeronautics Authority held a lease to install an airplane beacon on top
New telephone installed in the tower and a new line run from the tower to the camp (1953-54 report)
Hikers found the tower fallen from its cement base; a February 15, 1973 photo caption says the bolts appeared to have been purposely removed

notes_for_editor: Record height 18.3 m (60 ft) matches the 1924-38 wood tower. The 1938 steel tower was 80 ft (about 24.4 m), so height_m was left out of facts. The Mt. Philo Inn's 50-foot wooden tower is a separate account and may or may not be the same structure. The 1924 land gift is 150 acres in the state park's history but 160 acres in the 1924 Forest Lookouts item; the story uses 150 and cites the park. The 1973 bolts-removed explanation rests on one photo caption; treat the cause as unconfirmed. Forest Lookouts marks the tower 'Removed' and FFLA marks it 'Tower Gone'. No recent photo or site report was found, and no source describes footings. Record lat/lon was not checked against any source.
